title: Bay Area nursing homes mostly owed by related companies, year by year since 2012
question: In each year, how many Bay Area nursing homes carried half or more of their assets as money owed by related companies?
finding: 32 of 192 Bay Area skilled-nursing homes met the test in 2015 ($479.8 million); 44 of 187 in 2021 ($725.5 million); 42 of 182 in 2025. The years 2020 and 2021, missing from the case, sit on the same rising line.
how: Every Bay Area skilled-nursing home with a report that year (complete data sets 2015-2025; pivot profiles 2012-2014), with the case's test: net amount owed by related parties at least half of total assets and at least $3 million.
limits: The count rises partly because chains bought homes and moved their cash into central accounts, which is ordinary treasury practice. Homes that report under a new licence after a sale are counted again under the new number. 2023 to 2025 are unaudited.
